p: third year: After that he departed from the river Cherith.
feared the LORD greatly: God had begun to work his fear in his heart, but had not yet brought him to the knowledge which is also required of the godly: that is, to profess his Name openly.
met him: God often pities the wicked for the sake of the godly, and causes Elijah to meet with Obadiah, that the blessing might be known to be granted for the sake of God's children.
fear the LORD from my youth: I am not of the wicked persecutors that you should procure to me such displeasure, but serve God and favour his children.
myself unto him to day: By my presence I will declare that you have told him the truth.
thou: The true ministers of God should not only not permit falsehoods, but should boldly reprove the wicked slanderers without respect of persons.
halt ye between two opinions: Be consistent in religion and do not be indifferent, whether you follow God or Baal, or whether you serve God wholly or in part, Zep 1:5.
by fire: By sending down fire from heaven to burn the sacrifice.
leaped upon the altar which was: As men possessed by some strange spirit.
awaked: He mocks their beastly madness, who think that by any instance or suit, the dead and vile idols can help their worshippers in their necessity.

filled the trench also with water: By this he declared the excellent power of God, who contrary to nature could make the fire burn even in the water, so that they should have no opportunity to doubt that he is the only God.
again: Though God permits his to run in blindness and error for a time, yet eventually he calls them home to him by some notorious sign and work.
one of them escape: He commanded them that as they were truly persuaded to confess the only God: so they should serve him with all their power, and destroy the idolaters his enemies.
seven times: As God's spirit moved him to pray, so was he strengthened by the same that he did not faint, but continued still till he had obtained.
before Ahab to the entrance of: He was so strengthened by God's spirit that he ran faster than the chariot was able to run.
